prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can I get a dry red wine that's light with some spices and a warming feel, to go with a spicy curry?"

List A:
Wine 1: Rosé, France, $10. Tasting note: "This perfumed, spicy wine has crisp red fruit and acidity. Light and with a soft aftertaste, it's attractive and ready to drink."
Wine 2: Merlot, US, $86. Tasting note: "This full-bodied, voluptuous wine is spicy in red fruit and floral aromas that lend it a finessed, elegant air. Soft and round, with structure and acidity, it ends in bittersweet chocolate and clove. Drink now through 2023."
Wine 3: Pinot Noir, France, $28. Tasting note: "Very pale in color, this spice and red-fruit flavored wine is refreshing and crisp. It's a light wine, cut through by acidity and floral undertones. Drink this attractive wine now."
Wine 4: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $15. Tasting note: "A soft and ripe wine with spicy red fruit flavors cushioned by a smooth texture, this has well-embedded tannins and can be drunk young."
Wine 5: Gewürztraminer, US, $20. Tasting note: "Fresh and delicate with floral and citrus overtones, this wine has an elegant character. Its dry, spicy flavors are subtle and refreshing, giving the wine food pairing flexibility. Ideally, though, think of spicy cuisine like Indian, Thai or Indonesian."

List B:
Wine 1: Red Blend, Greece, $40. Tasting note: "The spicy, warm nose on this mellow red is an apt start to a really good wine. Flavors of clove, cinnamon and spice mingle with red berry and a slight tingle on the tongue and finish. An intriguing sip that will pair well with dishes of like warming spice: think Moroccan, Turkish."
Wine 2: Pinotage, South Africa, $10. Tasting note: "Cherry, pepper and spice on the nose are followed by similar flavors in this dry red. Balanced and touched with oak, the wine will pair well with grilled meats and spiced dishes. For fans of softer wines, age this for a few years before drinking."
Wine 3: Xinomavro, Greece, $26. Tasting note: "Plum, spice and cedar lead this spicy red. The wine offers bright but balanced flavors of red and black cherry, cedar and warming spice. The finish has a clean, mineral edge. Pair this with strong cheeses and dried meats."
Wine 4: Red Blend, US, $27. Tasting note: "Spiced meats, cherry and pepper give this plucky red a food-friendly edge. On the palate, it's spicy and slightly tart, with cranberry, blueberry and crushed herbs. Earthy and dry, the wine will pair well with spiced meat and pastas."
Wine 5: Pinot Noir, France, $26. Tasting note: "This light-colored wine has a spicy character that points up the tannins as well as the red berry fruits. It has a light feeling, with refreshing acidity that shows strongly at the end. It's ready to drink."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
